title: Volume spikes
prompt: Surveillance flags days when a stock trades far more shares than on its previous trading row. Write `solve(daily_prices)` so it returns the days whose `volume` is more than twice the previous row's volume for the same symbol.
rules: The previous row is the same `symbol`'s row with the latest earlier `trade_date`.
A spike is a `volume` of more than 2 × the previous volume. Exactly twice doesn't count.
A symbol's first row has nothing to compare with, so it is never a spike.
hints: First add the previous volume to every row with `F.lag` over a window per symbol in date order.
Then filter on the new column. A comparison with a missing value isn't true, so first rows drop out on their own.
Name the lagged value with `alias` so `filter` can compare against it. "More than twice" is a strict `>` against the previous volume times 2.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

    # The days with more than twice the previous row's volume.
